facts.text: Villa Verde emerged as a small agricultural community in Hidalgo County during the early 20th century, building on earlier Spanish land grants in the Rio Grande Valley.
The Ballí San Antonio del Esterito Ranch, founded around 1839 by the Ballí family, was the first major cattle operation on the land that would become Villa Verde.
The Ballí Cemetery, with its earliest marked grave from 1874, remains a tangible link to the ranching heritage that shaped the area.
In the 1920s, irrigation projects turned arid ranchlands into fertile farms, sparking rapid settlement in Villa Verde.
The Farm-to-Market road system, launched in 1943, added FM 88 and FM 491, improving market access and reducing flood risks for Villa Verde.
Villa Verde sits on a flat alluvial plain about 75 feet above sea level, where rich loam soils support the region’s year‑long growing season.
